name: mlua-serde-paths
instr:
Please add opt-in error paths to mlua's Serde conversion of Lua configuration values in `/app`, targeting Lua 5.4 with `lua54,vendored,async,serde,macros`. Errors should identify the offending value rather than just its type. Don't add new crates.

Add the public field `mlua::serde::DeserializeOptions::track_path: bool` (default `false`), the builder method `pub const fn mlua::serde::DeserializeOptions::track_path(self, enabled: bool) -> Self`, and `pub fn mlua::SerializableValue::track_path(self, enabled: bool) -> Self`. Both builders can enable or disable tracking. Tracking applies to `LuaSerdeExt::from_value_with`, `mlua::serde::Deserializer::new_with_options`, and serialization through `Value::to_serializable()`.

When enabled, prefix an error's original message exactly once with `path: `. Deserialization errors remain `Error::DeserializeError`; serialization passes that prefixed message to the target serializer's custom error. A failure at the root uses `$`. Nested paths omit `$`: for example, a bad port produces `servers[2].port: invalid type: string "bad", expected u16`.

Paths follow the original Lua structure. Sequence and tuple indices are one-based, including entries skipped by permissive options. Map string keys matching ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` use dot-separated names; other strings use brackets containing their Rust `Debug` representation. Examples are `alpha`, `_ok9`, `["9bad"]`, and `["café"]`. Integer and boolean keys use `[value]`; other keys use `[?]`
